candidate.answerReason: The triangle has area 4. Requiring the region to the right of the cut to have area 2 gives the unique admissible cut x=3, agreeing with choice B.

methods.label: Find the area to the right of the cut
methods.explanation:
The horizontal side from \((1,1)\) to \((9,1)\) has length \(8\), and its corresponding height is \(1\). Thus the triangle's area is \(\frac12\cdot8\cdot1=4\), so each region must have area \(2\).

Write the cutting line as \(x=t\). The part of the triangle with \(x\le1\) fits inside a unit square, so its area is at most \(1\). Therefore an equal-area cut must have \(t>1\). It must also have \(t<9\), since otherwise the region to its right has zero area.

The side through \((0,0)\) and \((9,1)\) has equation \(y=kx\), where \(9k=1\), so \(y=x/9\). Consequently, the region to the right of \(x=t\) is a right triangle with horizontal leg \(9-t\) and vertical leg \(1-t/9\). Its area must satisfy
\[
\frac12(9-t)\left(1-\frac t9\right)=2,
\]
which simplifies to
\[
(9-t)^2=36.
\]
Because \(t<9\), the length \(9-t\) is positive, so \(9-t=6\) and \(t=3\). This lies in \((1,9)\) and gives the required area \(2\). The line is \(\boxed{x=3.0}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).

methods.label: Compare similar right triangles
methods.explanation:
Let \(O=(0,0)\), \(A=(1,1)\), and \(B=(9,1)\). The area of \(OAB\) is \(\frac12\cdot8\cdot1=4\), so each desired region has area \(2\).

Write the cut as \(x=t\). For \(t\le1\), the left-hand region fits inside a unit square and cannot have area \(2\). For \(t\ge9\), the right-hand region has zero area. Hence \(1<t<9\).

Add the point \(C=(0,1)\). The enclosing right triangle \(BCO\) has area \(\frac12\cdot9\cdot1=9/2\). Let the cut meet \(CB\) at \(P=(t,1)\) and \(OB\) at \(Q\). The right-hand region is triangle \(BPQ\). It is similar to \(BCO\), since both have a right angle and share the angle at \(B\).

For similar triangles, the area ratio is the square of the corresponding side ratio. Therefore
\[
\left(\frac{BP}{BC}\right)^2
=\frac{2}{9/2}=\frac49.
\]
Lengths are positive, so \(BP/BC=2/3\). Since \(BC=9\), we get \(BP=6\), placing \(P\) at horizontal coordinate \(9-6=3\). This cut gives a right-hand area of \(2\), and therefore equal halves. The answer is \(\boxed{x=3.0}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
